messages:
emma: FYI vuln triage asked to keep some packet captures for 14 days instead of the usual 7. They say the exploit chain needs more historical packets to repro. Can we scope an exception? :alarm_clock:
lia: Are we talking about raw PCAP blobs that live in object storage and also get a SIEM export index? Those are expensive and contain PII.
oscar: Correct. The triage case: payloads are split across sessions so session logs weren't enough. They requested a one-off 14d retention for specific capture IDs.
emma: Two immediate concerns: (1) who can request/unlock them (RBAC), (2) KMS unwrap rights and audit trail.
kai: My take: allow timeboxed exceptions but gate them with JIT unwrap via kms-proxy + approval workflow + MFA. No permanent role that can always unwrap.
maria: Legal: any retention extension should be justified and recorded. Exports leaving infra must be redacted. We need mandatory `justification` and `export_flag` in the ticket.
lia: Proposed flow (rough):
 - triage tags object with metadata tag `retain:14d:pcap`
 - creates ticket in security queue with severity + justification
 - approver (depending on severity) authorizes unwrap window (mins)
 - kms-proxy issues ephemeral unwrap token and logs event to audit-main
 - if files are to be exported, run scrubber + DLP, record export artifact id

security-bot: draft policy stub -> https://internal.runbooks.company/pcap-ephemeral-retain (DRAFT) :link:
okai: sample kms-proxy config we sketched:
```
pcap_policy:
  default: 7d
  allowed_exception_days: 14d
  approver_roles:
    low: sec-triage-lead
    high: soc-manager + legal
  require_mfa: true
  require_justification: true
  kms_cmk_alias: alias/redwood-pcap
  unwrap_max_minutes: 120
  audit_event_type: pcap:access:grant
```

oscar: Audit volume is a big one. Let's emit a single composite audit event per grant that contains ticket_id, user, role, duration, key_version, file_ids. That keeps SIEM index small but linkable.
lia: Agree. Event schema fields: user, role, ticket_id, severity, file_count, key_version, unwrap_until, approver. We'll keep it compact and store the full JSON blob in audit-main but only index a subset in SIEM.
emma: KMS rotation question: if CMK rotates while retained objects still encrypted, can proxy still unwrap? We should avoid complex key-unwrap chains.
kai: Plan: background rewrap job that re-encrypts retained PCAPs onto the new key within N hours of rotation. Add a migration tag so rewrap happens automatically. If rewrap fails, alert sec-ops.
maria: Also: retention extensions for customer-related incidents need product security + legal sign-off. No unilateral dev approval.
oscar: Emergency path: SOC lead can escalate and get a temporary grant with post-facto review within 24h. All escalations auto-create a high-priority ticket and notify legal.
lia: Ticket template fields we should require: requester, owner, ticket_id, justification, severity, file_ids/time-window, requested_extra_days, approver(s), export_allowed (y/n), scrub_required (y/n).
security-bot: checklist added to runbook. Reminder: any export must pass DLP and be approved by legal.
emma: Can we add a `--no-export` flag in CLI to explicitly block export for that grant? That would help triage keep raw bytes but prevent accidental sharing.
kai: Will implement. CLI example:
```
redwood-kms-proxy grant-unwrap --ticket 6789 --files f123,f234 --minutes 60 --mfa --reason "repro exploit chain" --no-export
```

oscar: For SIEM, I will create a compact dashboard that surfaces counts of `pcap:access:grant` and top requesters. We'll keep raw audit JSON in audit-main for deep dives.
lia: We should also add an automated scrubber pipeline stage that can run as a pre-export hook. Scrubber rules: hash/eat emails, mask IPs per policy, strip payloads matching regex for SSN/CC.
maria: Legal: good. Add retention justification field and a checkbox if customer data may be impacted. We'll require Legal review if checkbox checked.
security-bot: action items recorded: [kai: implement proxy changes + CLI flags (ETA 3d), lia: draft approver matrix + ticket template (ETA 2d), oscar: SIEM event schema + dashboard (ETA 4d), security-bot: publish runbook draft and checklist].
emma: One more: limit on number of concurrent unwrap grants per user/team to avoid bulk exfil. Maybe 3 active grants max.
kai: Will enforce concurrency limit in proxy. Also add rate-limit to request endpoint and alert if thresholds hit.
oscar: We'll also index a tiny `grant_summary` doc in SIEM with ticket_id, user, file_count, unwrap_until to make searches cheap. Full audit remains in audit-main.
lia: OK. Let's reconvene in #eng-security in 3 days to sign off on the runbook. Post updates in the doc channel. :thumbsup:
emma: Thanks. tagging the vuln triage lead to set expectations.
security-bot: Reminder: all changes require a config review and will go through change control. :lock:
